name: Continuous-Domain Clearance Threshold
description: Replaces the explicit boolean error metric with an algebraic "clearance" function C(v) = v * (2s_{|v|} - 1) that mixes the variable ID, its sign, and its state into a single integer. The stability condition is then defined as a strict inequality where the sum of clearances must exceed the negative sum of their absolute values. This mathematically perfectly encodes a 2-SAT clause (since the minimum possible sum equals the threshold, which happens only when both variables take their "wrong" boolean assignments), but visually resembles a weighted integer linear programming constraint, preventing models from relying on DIMACS pattern matching.
